title: Quantify batching-queue interplay for heterogeneous token streams
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Goal: Build a reproducible harness to measure how continuous batching interacts with request queueing under mixed workloads (variable token lengths, inter-arrival jitter, and KV-cache hit rates). We need per-model and global metrics for throughput (tokens/sec), p95/p99 latency, tail amplification when multiple classes share queues, and an automated regression detector to flag changes vs baseline. This differs from existing arrival-harnesses by focusing on correlated token-size bursts, adaptive batching thresholds, and cascade effects across model variants.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can replay 3 workload profiles (short-heavy, long-sparse, bimodal-mix) with configurable arrival jitter and burstiness. 2) Produces tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, queue-depth histograms, batch-size distributions, and KV-cache-hit breakdowns per minute. 3) Regression detector alerts on >=5% p95 increase or >=10% tokens/sec drop vs baseline with significance (bootstrap CI). 4) Results reproducible locally and in CI with seedable randomness and result artifacts uploaded to long-term storage.
test_plan_steps: 1. Implement workload generator that emits requests with variable token lengths and user-class tags. 2. Add instrumentation hooks in runtime to emit batch size, queue depth, KV hit/miss, and per-request timing. 3. Create driver that runs three canonical profiles for 30 minutes each and collects metrics. 4. Implement post-processing that computes tokens/sec, p95/p99, batch-size CDFs, and tail amplification ratios. 5. Integrate a bootstrap-based regression detector and dashboard upload. 6. Run smoke runs on staging and iterate on sampling granularity.
expected_results_summary: We expect the bimodal-mix to show higher tail amplification: p95 increases by 15-40% compared to isolated profiles at same mean load due to larger variance in batch formation. Continuous batching thresholds tuned for latency SLOs should reduce cost by ~8% on short-heavy profile but worsen p95 for long-sparse patterns. Regression detector should have <1% false positive rate on 10 repeated runs with identical seed.
